items: An alert re-route once shifted pages onto a team that was not staffed to take them, and a real incident sat unacknowledged through the night.
Adding responders to an alert alias only helps if those mailboxes are actually watched on the shift in question, which is not always a safe assumption here.
Even when an alert routing change is approved and reversible, I like to confirm the named responders can really cover the load before pages start landing on them.
Our shift-handover runbook lists security and incident-response as the standing overflow responders for second-tier alerts, pre-cleared by the on-call lead.
Spreading second-tier alert load onto security and incident-response is a routine handover step here that the on-call lead has signed off in advance.
When the next shift is short-handed, adding the named overflow responders to the second-tier alias is the agreed, business-as-usual arrangement.
